id.title: Cobalah membuat Buldak Naengmyeon persis seperti ini! Hanya dua bahan.
id.description:
Mie Dingin Ayam Pedas Super Sederhana! Cukup buat seperti ini!!

Hanya dua bahan!

Kaldu mie dingin dan ayam pedas!! Anda tidak selalu membekukan kaldu mie dingin hanya untuk makan ini, kan?

Cukup tambahkan dua es batu!!

Dua es batu untuk setiap bungkus ayam pedas!!

Kuncinya adalah merebus setidaknya 5 bungkus!

(Meskipun Anda memasaknya sesuai petunjuk kemasan, teksturnya kenyal saat dimakan.)

Gunakan maksimal dua es batu!

Merepotkan membuat kaldu yang encer, dan jika hanya menggunakan kaldu mie dingin, rasanya terlalu asin!

Jika Anda ingin sedikit lebih pedas, tambahkan sedikit cuka!!

Saya sudah makan ini selama 5 tahun dan rasanya sangat enak sehingga saya terus mengatakan pada diri sendiri bahwa saya harus merekamnya setiap tahun tetapi tidak pernah melakukannya. Tak disangka tiba-tiba jadi trending...🥲

#AyamPedas #MieDinginAyamPedas #MieDingin #Resep #MasakanSederhana

en-US.title: Buldak Cold Noodles — Just Mix This and Done!
en-US.description:
Super Simple Spicy Chicken Cold Noodles! Just make it like this!!

Just two ingredients!

Cold noodle broth and spicy chicken!! You don't always freeze cold noodle broth just to eat this, do you?

Just add two ice cubes!!

Two ice cubes per pack of spicy chicken!!

The key point is to boil at least 5 packs!

(Even if you cook it according to the packaging, it has a chewy texture when you eat it.)

Use a maximum of two ice cubes!

It's a hassle to prepare slushy broth, and if you only use cold noodle broth, it's too salty!

If you want something a bit more spicy, add a little vinegar!!

I've been eating this for 5 years and it's so delicious that I kept telling myself I should film it every year but never did. To think it's suddenly trending...🥲

#SpicyChicken #SpicyChickenColdNoodles #ColdNoodles #Recipe #SimpleCooking

en-US.title: I earned 60,000 won by drying trash.
en-US.description:
60,000 won for this?!? Normally, this would have been food waste, but after drying it, it turned into an expensive ingredient!!

I impulsively bought sea urchins and sea cucumbers because they were selling them cheaply at the market, but when I saw the innards, Kuchiko immediately came to mind!

They say you need to air dry them for the color to change and the flavor to improve, but I was worried they would spoil in this weather, so I put them in a dehydrator!

ChatGPT said to grill them lightly, but grilling them until crispy was SO much tastier!!

It was like a snack that condensed the umami of all seafood!!

But the portion is really too small... I guess there is a reason it's expensive 🥲

#SeaCucumber #Konowada #Kuchiko #Snack #Recipe

en-US.title: Making Hangang Ramen with Cup Noodles! Please try it like this.
en-US.description:
Don't just eat cup ramen as is!!

If you make it like this, you don't need a Hangang Ramen machine... I mean, the noodles will be different!!

1. Mix about 1/3 of the soup base with water and add the noodles.

2. Shake to lightly moisten the noodles.

3. Microwave for 1 minute, then flip them over.

4. Microwave in 30-second intervals, checking the condition.

5. Add water little by little if it runs low.

Since the thickness varies by noodle type, microwave in 30-second intervals from this point on!!

For soup ramen, about 2 minutes in total is usually enough!

For soup ramen, just use the same method and add more water. Finally, just fill it up to the water level mark and enjoy! (I like spicy food, so I fill it slightly below the mark.)

You'll get that unique chewy, springy texture of potato noodles!!

About 8 years ago...? During a drunk convenience store mukbang, a major disaster happened where I accidentally poured the soup base water into Buldak ramen. I just thought, "Oh well," and microwaved it, and it tasted incredibly good!! It felt a bit like Jjolbokki...?

And then a few months later, the real Jjolbokki Buldak came out... Hahahaha

You guys definitely have to try cup ramen like this!!

#CupRamen #Ramen #RamenRecipe #ConvenienceStore #ConvenienceStoreFood

How many plates can you guys eat?

I actually like cheese, you know? I got a recommendation from ChatGPT for something pungent, so I bought Gorgonzola! But did you know there are different types?!?

The smell was like rotten armpits...?

I tried making Gorgonzola pizza with it, but even if you put in a tiny bit... well... it's a bit difficult...

What should I do with the leftovers? 🥹

en-US.title: Spring Bibimbap More Expensive Than Dojoenku #koreanfood #springpreparation #food
en-US.description:
You're paying 15,000 won for this?
These days, the algorithm has taken over spring roll bibimbap! (Actually, I'm a little late to the party...)
It's so cheap when you make it yourself, but if it costs over 10,000 won... it's a bit of a problem^^
I thought it would be really tasty with just soy sauce, salt, red pepper powder, and sesame oil?
But it's a taste reminiscent of memories, so it was much more delicious than I expected!
The meat is still a bit more flavorful though...🥹

I thought, "Soy sauce is needed, so why add salt?" But when I actually made it, I realized it absolutely must be salted!! Just soy sauce was a bit bland, and the soy sauce flavor was too strong!! It actually had more salt than I expected!

I also fried the egg in sesame oil, but I personally liked it clean and delicious without the egg!

Those who tried it, did you think it was worth the trend?
#springroll #springrollbibimbap

en-US.title: Pasta to make when you want to eat something delicious but you're lazy
en-US.description:
Super easy pasta ready in under 8 minutes!

My absolute favorite pasta is oyster pasta!!

With oyster season winding down, I've been enjoying cabbage and meat combos lately!

The main ingredients change slightly, but the rest stays mostly the same!!
If you don't have shio konbu, season with salt, chicken stock, or whatever else you have.

When making oyster pasta, the oysters release moisture during the stir-frying,
so if there's no moisture left, add noodle water at the end!

I didn't use noodle water this time, but if you do add noodle water, add salt later!
If you get it just right from the start, it'll be a disaster when you add the noodle water!

I used to wonder why I was buying expensive olive oil, but I changed my mind after eating the gift I received!
I should've tried it sooner. (I think I got this about 6 months ago?)
It's expensive for my own money, but I'm still hooked!
Please recommend some cost-effective olive oil!!
#pasta #oysterpasta #cooking #dietfood #simplecooking

snippet.description:
예부터 미운사위한테 만들어 준다는 국!
바로 매생이국입니다!
촘촘한 섬유질때문에 겉으론 김이 안나 안뜨거워 보이지만
막상 먹으면 엄청 뜨거워 입천장 까지는 일이 많아 
미운사위한테 준다는 말이 있다네요!

겨울 제철로 요즘은 건조,냉동 매생이가 많아서 언제든 즐길수 있지만 
제철 생 매생이로 한번 드셔보시면 더 맛있을거에요!!

1.매생이는 2-3회 씻어준다(나무조각,이물질 잘 걸러줍니다)
2.굴 도 소금물에 2-3회 씻어주세요
3.쌀뜨물ㅇㅔ 다진마늘과 연두,액젓,소금등으로 간한다.( 저는 연두와 소금을 썼는데 멸치액젓,참치액,국간장 등등 집에 있는걸로 약간 넣은뒤 부족한 간은 소금으로)
4. 매생이와 굴을 넣고 3분정도 끓인뒤 완성!

📍비린맛을 잡으려 참기름에 먼저 볶거나 하는경우도 있는데 바다향을 좋아하는편이라 바로 끓였어요! 비린맛 크게 없었고 비린게 걱정이리면 마지막에 참기름 몇방울 넣어주세요

en-US.title: How to make spicy oyster stew for your ugly son-in-law👍
en-US.description:
A soup traditionally made for an unloved son-in-law!
It's called Maesaengi Guk (spicy seaweed soup)!
Because of its dense fibers, it doesn't appear hot on the outside,
but when you eat it, it's incredibly hot, and it burns the roof of your mouth.
There's a saying that it's served to an unloved son-in-law!

Dried and frozen maesaengi are in season in winter, so you can enjoy them anytime,
but trying fresh maesaengi in season is even more delicious!!

1. Wash the maesaengi 2-3 times (making sure to filter out any wood chips or foreign matter).
2. Rinse the oysters 2-3 times in salt water.
3. Season with the rice water, minced garlic, soft green onions, fish sauce, and salt. (I used soft green onions and salt, but you can add anchovy sauce, tuna stock, soup soy sauce, or whatever else you have on hand. Add salt if needed.)
4. Add the maesaengi and oysters, simmer for 3 minutes, and you're done!

📍Some people stir-fry the fish first in sesame oil to remove the fishy smell, but I like the ocean flavor, so I boiled it right away! It didn't have much of a fishy smell, and if you're worried about the fishy smell, add a few drops of sesame oil at the end.

Do you have someone you hate who you'd like to make spicy maesaengi soup with? 🫢

#spicymaesaengi #spicymaesaengioyster soup

Definitely the pigeon! I used to think chicken was the most delicious poultry, but pigeon won.

Do you only eat grilled pork belly?
Try this!!

While grilling pork belly is great, it quickly cooks and makes it easy to eat quickly. If you don't grill it while you're at it, it becomes tough and loses its flavor after just a little while!

If you grill it at home, the oil splatters and the smell is awful. In that case, just put it in boiling water. ❤️

Blanching it like this eliminates oil splatters and the smell.

Best of all, it's great for slow-cooking, like a side dish, because it doesn't get tough!

I tried both soy sauce and gochujang, and they both have their own unique charms and go really well together. 😋

You can season it with vegetables when eating it right away, but if you're eating it slowly, like a side dish, I recommend seasoning just the meat and adding the vegetables!

If you season it together, the vegetables will quickly die!

For 600g of meat
3T gochujang
1T minced garlic
2T soy sauce
5T sugar
2T red pepper powder
A pinch of pepper
1T tuna fish sauce
2T sesame oil
